title: SSH — Remote Access
objective: Understand how SSH works, connect to remote machines, learn about SSH keys, and copy files securely with scp.
explanation: What if you could control your Raspberry Pi from another computer — without even being in the same room? That is exactly what SSH does. SSH stands for Secure Shell, and it lets you open a terminal on a remote computer over the network. Everything you type is encrypted, which means nobody can spy on your commands or passwords as they travel across the internet. To connect to another machine, you type ssh followed by your username, the at sign, and the address of the remote computer: ssh youngster@192.168.1.50. If it is your first time connecting, SSH will ask you to confirm the remote computer's identity by showing a fingerprint. Type yes. Then it asks for your password. Once you are in, everything looks like a normal terminal, but every command you type runs on the remote machine, not your local one. To leave the remote session, type exit. Typing your password every time can get tedious, and it is also less secure. That is why SSH supports key-based authentication. An SSH key is a pair of files: a private key (which stays on your computer and you never share) and a public key (which you put on the remote machine). When you connect, the two keys work together to prove your identity without a password. You create keys with ssh-keygen and copy the public key to the remote machine with ssh-copy-id. Once that is done, you can log in without typing a password. SSH also comes with a file-copying tool called scp (secure copy). It works like cp, but across the network. To copy a file to a remote machine: scp myfile.txt youngster@192.168.1.50:/home/youngster/. To download a file from a remote machine: scp youngster@192.168.1.50:/home/youngster/data.txt ./. The colon separates the address from the file path. SSH is one of the most important tools in the Linux world. Every server on the internet is managed through SSH. When you learn it, you unlock the ability to manage computers anywhere in the world from your terminal.

challenge.question: You want to connect to a Raspberry Pi on your network at 192.168.1.100 with the username 'pi'. What SSH command would you type?
challenge.hint: The format is ssh username@address. Replace the username and address with the ones given.

funFact: SSH was created in 1995 by a Finnish researcher named Tatu Ylonen after a password-sniffing attack at his university. Before SSH, people used Telnet, which sent everything — including passwords — as plain text that anyone on the network could read!
